title: Customer Accounts

brief.md:
- **Cold calls** (non-customers only): **8:00 am – 9:00 pm in the prospect’s local time**. Caller must give name + firm, phone + address, and purpose of the call.
- Scripts = **retail communications** → principal approval **before first use**.
- **Do-not-call**: the firm’s internal list is **indefinite**; the national registry also applies. Exceptions: **existing customer, personal relationship, prior written consent**.
- An unregistered employee may cold-call, but must **hand the call to a registered person** once the prospect wants more information.
- **New account form** (Rule 4512): name, address, phone, SSN/TIN, DOB, employment, citizenship, income, net worth (excl. home), tax bracket, objectives, experience, risk tolerance.
- **Only the designated principal signs** the form (not the customer, not the rep). Approval **before or promptly after** the first trade.
- Customer refuses to give financial data → account **can** open, but the rep can take **unsolicited orders only**.
- **Numbered account**: symbol or number, never an alias — but the firm still needs **written ownership statement + ID**.
- **Verification of information**: first request within **30 days** of opening; again within 30 days of any change; then **every 36 months** (each owner of a joint account).
> **Exam tip** Introducing firm = relationship + takes orders. Clearing firm = custody + settlement.

brief.h: Cash accounts, Reg T and free-riding
brief.md:
- **Cash account**: pay **in full**. Regular-way settlement is **T+1**.
- **Reg T payment deadline**: **2 business days after settlement (S+2)**. If unpaid and no extension: position **sold out** and account **frozen 90 days** (shortage ≤ **$1,000** → firm has discretion).
- **Frozen account**: sells allowed; buys only if the cash is **already in the account** when the order is placed.
- **Free-riding** = buying and selling a security **without ever paying** for it. Consequence: freeze (90 days) — proceeds are not released until the original purchase is paid.
> **Exam tip** Free-riding is about *never paying*. Paying late within the extension is not free-riding.

- Borrow from the broker-dealer; securities are the **collateral**. **All short sales must be in a margin account.**
- **Reg T initial margin = 50%** (since 1974). Government and municipal securities are **exempt from Reg T** → margin set by FINRA.
- **FINRA minimum equity** for small trades:

| Trade size | Long | Short |
|---|---|---|
| Up to $2,000 | **100%** of price | **$2,000** |
| $2,000 – $4,000 | **$2,000** | **$2,000** |
| Over $4,000 | **50%** (Reg T) | **50%** (Reg T) |

- **Maintenance**: **25%** of long market value, **30%** of short market value. **Marked to market daily.** Below requirement → **maintenance (margin) call**; firm may liquidate if unmet.
- **Eligible**: listed stocks, approved OTC, bonds, CEFs, ETFs, **LEAPS > 9 months**, Treasuries.
- **Not eligible**: **IPOs (first 30 days)**, unapproved OTC, **mutual funds**, options ≤ 9 months, annuities. Mutual funds can be *collateral* after **30 days**.
- **Margin agreement** = **hypothecation** (pledge; securities held in **street name**; **re-hypothecation** allowed) + **credit agreement** (interest = broker call + spread, lower rate for larger debit) + **loan consent** (**optional** — lets the firm lend your shares for short sales).
- **Margin disclosure statement** (Rule 2264): before/at opening, **annually**. Key warnings: lose more than you deposit; forced sale **without contacting you**; no say in what is sold; house requirements can rise **with no notice**; no right to an extension.

1. Customer expresses interest → rep sends the **options disclosure document** (ODD, prepared by the **OCC**) **at or before** approval.
2. A **Registered Options Principal (ROP)** reviews and approves **in writing** (level depends on profile: covered calls < naked options).
3. Customer **may start trading** once approved.
4. **Options agreement** must be signed and returned **within 15 days of approval**; otherwise **closing transactions only** (no new positions, no exercise).
> **Exam tip** Trading can begin *before* the signed agreement comes back. That surprises people.

- **Discretion = the rep decides any of the 3 A’s**: **A**ction (buy/sell), **A**sset (which security), **A**mount (how many). **Time and price are not discretionary** (a “time and price” order is *not held*).
- Needs **written power of attorney** (Rule 2510) + principal approval **before the first trade**, and **prompt** approval of each discretionary trade.
- POA **ends at death**. Court-declared incompetence cancels it unless it is a **durable** POA.
- **Signature of convenience** (signing for the client) is prohibited, even with permission.
- **Churning** = excessive trading inconsistent with objectives to generate commissions (no fixed trade count).
- **Fee-based accounts**: unsuitable for **buy-and-hold / infrequent traders**.
- **DVP / RVP**: settlement methods tying delivery of securities to payment.

brief.h: Account titles and what happens at death
brief.md:
| Account | At death of an owner | Probate |
|---|---|---|
| **Individual** | Open orders cancelled, account frozen → beneficiary, else will/estate | Yes (unless **TOD**) |
| **JTIC** (tenants in common) | **Their share** goes to their own beneficiary/estate | **Yes** |
| **JTWROS** | Interest passes to **surviving owners** | **No** |

- Joint accounts: unlimited owners, any owner can give instructions, **checks payable to all owners**. A **parent and minor child cannot** open a joint account.
- JTIC fits e.g. **two siblings who want assets to go to their own spouses**. JTWROS fits spouses / parent + adult child.

- **UGMA/UTMA**: adult **custodian** (fiduciary) manages for a minor. Securities in the **custodian’s name**; **minor’s SSN** on the account.
- **One custodian, one minor.** Donor need not be a parent; **donor can be the custodian**.
- **Gifts are irrevocable**; assets cannot move from one child’s account to another’s.
- Age of majority: **18 (UGMA)**, **18–25 (UTMA, by state)**.
- **No margin**; risky strategies (naked options, penny stocks) are *inappropriate*, not outright banned. **Minor owes the taxes**; custodian makes sure they’re paid. A minor **cannot trade**, even with permission.
- **Trust**: trustor creates, **trustee** (fiduciary, has trading discretion) manages for beneficiaries; firm needs a **copy of the trust agreement**. **Revocable** (trustor can change) vs **irrevocable**. Can be invalidated for **undue influence** or **lack of capacity**.
- **Inherited securities** get a **stepped-up basis** = value at date of death.

- **Corporate**: **corporate resolution** naming who can trade; margin only if the **charter** allows it. **No beneficiary** (unlimited life). Taxed as a separate entity.
- **Partnership**: **partnership agreement** says which partners can transact.
- **Investment clubs**: usually partnerships; many firms require a special investment-club account.

brief.h: Ongoing duties: statements, confirms, mail, records
brief.md:
| Item | Rule |
|---|---|
| **Account statements** | **Quarterly** if a position, balance or activity; **monthly** if the account holds **options or penny stocks**; none if empty and inactive |
| **Trade confirmations** | **At or before settlement.** Principal trade → show **mark-up/mark-down**; agency trade → show **commission** |
| **Muni confirms** (MSRB G-15) | Yield to worst, call/put features, accrued interest, yield and dollar price, AMT status |
| **Annual reports / proxies** | Issuer mails if shares are in the customer’s name; **firm forwards** if in **street name**; issuer reimburses costs |
| **Hold mail** | **Permitted, not required**; **written** request; **max 3 months** unless valid reason (**safety**, not convenience) |
| **Account records** | Kept **6 years after the account is closed** |

brief.h: Protecting customers: Reg S-P, custody, SIPC, FDIC, vulnerable investors
brief.md:
- **Reg S-P (privacy)**: notice at **opening and annually**; customers may **opt out** of sharing with **non-affiliates** (typically **30 days** to do so) but **not** where sharing is legally required (IRS, AML).
- **Custody**: customer assets must be **segregated**; mixing customer and firm assets = **commingling** (prohibited). No withdrawing customer funds without **written authorization**.
- **SIPC**: non-profit, **not a government agency**. Covers loss from **broker-dealer failure**, **not market losses**. **$500,000 per separate customer, max $250,000 cash.** Value fixed at the **bankruptcy filing date**. Above the limit → general creditor. Not covered: commodities/futures.
- **Separate customers**: individual, joint, trust, IRA, Roth IRA, minor’s account — each protected to the limit.
- **FDIC**: **bank deposits** only, **$250,000** per depositor per bank; backed by the **US government**. Does **not** cover securities, mutual funds or annuities — even bought at a bank.
- **Vulnerable investors** (65+, or 18+ with impairment): obtain a **trusted contact**; temporary hold on disbursements **15 business days**, +**10**, +**30** if reported to authorities (**55 total**).
- **Financial condition** (Rule 2261): on request, provide the firm’s **balance sheet**.

traps: **Margin buys and mutual funds.** Mutual funds are **never** bought on margin. They only become *collateral* after 30 days. Exchange-traded funds and CEFs are eligible.
**25% vs 30%.** Long = 25% of **long market value**. Short = 30% of **short market value**. Examiners swap them.
**Initial vs maintenance.** Initial = 50% (Reg T) with FINRA $2,000 floor. Maintenance = 25% / 30%. Don’t mix the two in a calculation.
**Small trades.** For a long purchase of $1,500 you deposit **$1,500**, not $750. For a short sale of $1,500 you deposit **$2,000**.
**Who signs the new account form?** Only the **designated principal**. Not the customer, not the rep.
**Options account timing.** You can trade **before** returning the agreement; you lose the right to open new positions **after 15 days** without it.
**Discretion is not time/price.** A client choosing *what* and *how many* but letting the rep pick the **timing or price** is still non-discretionary.
**JTIC vs JTWROS.** “Rights of survivorship” = survivor takes everything and probate is avoided. JTIC = deceased’s share goes to **their** heirs and **is** probated.
**UGMA/UTMA.** The **minor’s** SSN is on the account, the minor pays the tax, gifts are irrevocable, and there is **no margin**.
**SIPC ≠ insurance against losses.** It covers a **failed broker-dealer**, never market declines. $500k **including** max $250k cash — not $500k *plus* $250k.
**FDIC vs SIPC.** FDIC = bank deposits (not mutual funds, even from a bank). SIPC = securities and cash at a brokerage.
**Mail hold.** Convenience is **not** a valid reason for more than 3 months.
**Free-riding.** The violation is selling without ever paying. A late payment inside an approved extension is not free-riding.

formulas.name: Initial margin deposit
formulas.example: Short 1,000 sh at $12 = $12,000 → 50% = **$6,000**. Long $3,200 → FINRA floor **$2,000** (Reg T alone would be $1,600).

formulas.name: Long account: equity and call
formulas.rule: Equity = Long market value (LMV) − Debit balance.  Requirement = 25% × LMV.  Call = Requirement − Equity (if positive).

formulas.name: Short account: equity and call
formulas.rule: Credit balance = short proceeds + initial deposit.  Equity = Credit balance − Short market value (SMV).  Requirement = 30% × SMV.
formulas.example: Short 1,000 at $40 (credit $60,000). Price rises to $50 → SMV $50,000; equity $10,000; requirement $15,000 → **call $5,000**.

formulas.name: SIPC coverage
formulas.rule: Covered = securities + min(cash, $250,000), capped at $500,000, per separate customer.

formulas.name: Stepped-up basis (inheritance)
formulas.rule: Heir’s cost basis = market value at date of death.
formulas.example: Bought at $10, owner dies at $30, heir sells at $34 → gain = **$4**, not $24.

questions.q: A registered representative in New York wants to cold-call a prospect (not an existing customer) who lives in Los Angeles. What is the earliest time, New York time, that the call may be placed?
w: Wrong: this subtracts the time difference instead of adding it.
Wrong: no adjustment of one hour applies.
Wrong: 8:00 am is the limit in the prospect’s time zone, not New York’s.
Correct: 8:00 am Pacific is 11:00 am Eastern; the window runs on the called person’s local time.

questions.q: Which of the following allows a representative to call a person who is on the firm’s internal do-not-call list?
o: The person is an existing customer of the firm
A colleague says the person no longer minds
The call is made before 9:00 am
The person asked to be removed six months ago
w: Correct: existing customers, personal relationships and prior written consent are exceptions.
Wrong: only the person’s own written consent counts.
Wrong: calling hours do not override the do-not-call status.
Wrong: the internal list is indefinite; time does not remove anyone.

questions.q: A firm wants its representatives to use a script on cold calls. How is the script treated?
o: A retail communication that must be approved by a principal before first use
A communication that must be filed with the SEC before use
w: Wrong: cold calls target the public, not institutions.
Correct: scripts are retail communications requiring prior principal approval.
Wrong: correspondence is a different category and no prior approval is required for a scripted solicitation.
Wrong: the SEC does not pre-approve broker-dealer scripts.

questions.q: An unregistered employee of a broker-dealer cold-calls prospects and offers to send a free research report. A prospect asks for more information about the company. What must the employee do?
o: End the call; unregistered staff may not cold-call at all
Turn the call over to a registered person
Give the prospect the firm’s investment recommendation
w: Wrong: discussing the substance goes beyond what an unregistered person may do.
Wrong: unregistered employees may place cold calls, within limits.
Correct: the call must be handed to a registered person.
Wrong: recommendations are a registered activity.

questions.q: Who is required to sign the new account form?
o: The customer and the registered representative
Only the designated principal who approves the account
The customer and the designated principal
w: Wrong: neither of them needs to sign.
Correct: the principal’s signature documents approval and is the only one required.
Wrong: the customer’s signature is not required on the form itself.
Wrong: the customer need not sign the form.

questions.q: A new client provides all identification data but refuses to disclose income and net worth. What is true?
o: The account may be opened but the rep can only take unsolicited orders
The principal may approve recommendations after the first trade
The account may be opened and the rep may recommend conservative products
w: Correct: without the facts, no recommendations; only unsolicited orders.
Wrong: approval does not cure the lack of information.
Wrong: any recommendation requires knowing the customer’s facts.
Wrong: refusal does not prevent opening.

questions.q: A customer who wants anonymity from relatives at the firm asks to open an account. What may the firm do?
o: Open the account under an alias
Open it under a fictitious name with made-up data
Open a numbered account, keeping a written statement of ownership and ID
w: Wrong: aliases are not allowed.
Wrong: false information is never allowed.
Correct: a symbol or number is allowed, with ownership statement and proof of identity on file.
Wrong: numbered accounts are permitted.

questions.q: After the initial verification, how often must a firm send customers a request to verify their account information?
o: Only when the customer reports a change
w: Wrong: annual verification is not the rule; after the first request the interval is 36 months.
Wrong: periodic verification is mandatory even without a change.
Wrong: not the required interval.
Correct: the initial request within 30 days, then every 36 months (and 30 days after any reported change).

questions.q: Which function is performed by a clearing firm but not by an introducing firm?
o: Holding customer cash and securities and settling trades
w: Wrong: the introducing firm opens accounts.
Wrong: the introducing firm takes orders.
Correct: custody and settlement belong to the clearing firm.
Wrong: collected at the introducing level.

questions.q: A customer buys stock in a cash account and does not pay by the Reg T deadline; no extension is granted and the shortage exceeds $1,000. What happens?
o: The firm sells the position and freezes the account for 90 days
The firm freezes the account for 30 days only
The firm charges margin interest and keeps the position
The customer is reported to the SEC
w: Correct: sell-out and a 90-day freeze.
Wrong: the freeze is 90 days.
Wrong: a cash account has no margin loan.
Wrong: no automatic SEC report; the consequence is the sell-out and freeze.

questions.q: Susan buys ABC stock on Tuesday (regular way) and sells the same shares on Tuesday in a cash trade, using the proceeds to pay for her purchase. This is:
o: Permitted if she pays by settlement
w: Wrong: she never paid with her own money.
Correct: she bought and sold without paying for the stock — free-riding.
Wrong: no margin loan is involved.
Wrong: churning concerns excessive trading by a rep.

questions.q: An account is frozen for free-riding. Which orders are permitted?
o: Only orders approved by a principal
Sell orders, and buy orders only if full cash is in the account when placed
w: Wrong: approval is not the test; funding is.
Wrong: buys with cash already on deposit are also allowed.
Wrong: trading is limited, not banned.
Correct: sells, plus buys fully funded at the time of the order.

questions.q: A customer wants to sell stock short. In which account must the trade be placed?
w: Wrong: cash accounts require full payment for purchases and cannot hold shorts.
Correct: all short sales are executed in a margin account.
Wrong: custodial accounts cannot use margin.
Wrong: only margin accounts.

questions.q: A customer buys $60,000 of listed stock in a margin account. What is the minimum initial deposit?
w: Wrong: 75% is not a margin requirement.
Wrong: 25% is the maintenance level for longs.
Correct: Reg T requires 50% → $30,000.
Wrong: that is the cash-account requirement.

questions.q: A customer buys $3,200 of stock in a margin account. What is the minimum deposit?
w: Correct: between $2,000 and $4,000 the minimum is $2,000.
Wrong: 50% would be $1,600, but the FINRA minimum overrides it.
Wrong: the full price is required only at $2,000 or less.
Wrong: no such requirement.

questions.q: A customer buys $1,500 of stock in a margin account. What is the minimum deposit?
w: Wrong: 50% is less than the allowed purchase price.
Wrong: she doesn’t need to deposit more than the cost.
Wrong: 75% of the price is not a margin level; the FINRA rule is the lesser of $2,000 or 100%.
Correct: FINRA requires the lesser of $2,000 or 100% of the price → $1,500.

questions.q: A customer sells short 1,000 shares of XYZ at $12 and 100 shares of ABC at $10 in a margin account (two separate trades). What are the minimum deposits for each trade respectively?
w: Correct: $12,000 × 50% = $6,000; the $1,000 short needs the $2,000 minimum.
Wrong: the $12,000 short exceeds $4,000, so Reg T 50% applies.
Wrong: those are 100% figures.
Wrong: for a short sale of $1,000 the minimum is still $2,000.

questions.q: Which statement about Regulation T is correct?
o: It sets the maintenance requirement at 25%
It sets the initial margin requirement for margin-eligible securities
w: Wrong: Reg T is a Federal Reserve Board regulation.
Wrong: the 25% maintenance level is FINRA’s.
Wrong: municipals and governments are exempt from Reg T.
Correct: the Fed’s Reg T sets initial margin (50%).

questions.q: A customer’s long margin account holds $120,000 of securities. What is the FINRA minimum maintenance equity?
w: Wrong: 30% is the short requirement.
Wrong: 50% is the initial requirement.
Wrong: 100% is the cash-account level.

questions.q: A long margin account has market value of $60,000 and a debit balance of $48,000. How large is the maintenance call?
w: Wrong: equity is below the requirement.
Wrong: that is the equity, not the call.
Correct: equity = $12,000; requirement = 25% × $60,000 = $15,000; call = $3,000.
Wrong: that is the requirement, not the shortfall.

questions.q: A customer shorts 1,000 shares at $40 and deposits the initial requirement. The stock rises to $50. What is the maintenance call?
w: Wrong: misapplies the percentage.
Wrong: confuses requirement and initial deposit.
Correct: credit $60,000 − SMV $50,000 = equity $10,000; requirement 30% × $50,000 = $15,000; call $5,000.
Wrong: equity is below the requirement.

questions.q: How often are margin accounts marked to the market?
w: Wrong: the requirement is daily.
Wrong: weekly is too infrequent.
Wrong: monthly is not the rule.
Correct: daily, for both long and short accounts.

questions.q: Which of these can be purchased on margin?
o: A LEAPS option with 18 months to expiration
An IPO share 10 days after the effective date
w: Correct: LEAPS with more than 9 months to expiration are eligible.
Wrong: IPOs are restricted for the first 30 days.
Wrong: mutual funds cannot be bought on margin.
Wrong: annuities are not eligible.

questions.q: Which part of the margin agreement is optional for the customer to sign?
w: Wrong: sets interest terms; required.
Correct: it allows the firm to lend the customer’s shares for short sales.
Wrong: needed to pledge collateral.
Wrong: the loan consent is optional.

questions.q: By signing the hypothecation agreement, a margin customer:
o: Pledges securities as collateral for the margin loan
Allows the firm to sell shares at any time with no notice and no collateral
w: Correct: securities are pledged as collateral for the loan.
Wrong: not what hypothecation means.
Wrong: interest is set by the credit agreement.
Wrong: initial margin is 50% under Reg T.

questions.q: Which statement is NOT a required warning in the margin disclosure statement?
o: You can lose more than you deposit
The firm can sell your securities without contacting you
You are not entitled to an extension on a margin call
You will receive 30 days’ written notice before the firm raises house maintenance requirements
w: This warning is in the statement: a margin investor can lose more than the amount deposited.
This warning is in the statement: the firm may sell without contacting the customer.
This warning is in the statement: no entitlement to extra time on a margin call.
Correct choice: the warning is that the firm can raise requirements without advance notice.

questions.q: A customer wants to trade options. Which sequence is correct?
o: Signed agreement → principal approval → disclosure document
Disclosure document (at or before approval) → ROP approval → trading → signed agreement within 15 days
ROP approval → trading → disclosure document at 15 days
w: Wrong: the agreement comes after approval.
Correct: the ODD is delivered at or before approval; trading may begin; agreement due within 15 days.
Wrong: the ODD cannot be delayed.
Wrong: the agreement is not first.

questions.q: A customer’s options account was approved 20 days ago but the customer has not returned the signed options agreement. The customer may:
w: Wrong: closing is permitted.
Wrong: after 15 days new positions are not allowed.
Correct: liquidating (closing) transactions only.
Wrong: exercising is also barred.

questions.q: A client tells the rep: “I want exposure to technology.” The rep picks the specific stock and buys it. This trade is:
o: Non-discretionary because the client chose the sector
Discretionary because the rep chose the asset
w: Wrong: choosing the specific security is the rep’s decision.
Wrong: “not held” refers to time and price latitude.
Wrong: the client did not initiate the specific purchase.
Correct: deciding any of action, asset or amount makes it discretionary.

questions.q: A client tells the rep: “Buy 100 shares of Apple when the time and price are right.” The trade is:
w: Wrong: time and price are not discretionary items.
Wrong: nothing prohibits a client leaving time and price to the rep; it simply isn’t discretion.
Correct: action, asset and amount are set by the client.
Wrong: this is a single trade.

questions.q: Which is true of a power of attorney for discretionary trading?
o: It continues after the customer’s death
It must be written, and a principal must approve the account before the first trade
The rep may sign for the customer if permission is given
It is needed only for margin accounts
w: Wrong: a power of attorney ends at the customer’s death.
Correct: written authority, principal approval before first trade and promptly after each trade.
Wrong: signing for a customer is prohibited.
Wrong: it concerns discretion, not margin.

questions.q: Excessive trading in a conservative client’s account that earns the rep commissions is called:
w: Correct: excessive trading inconsistent with objectives to generate fees.
Wrong: mixing customer and firm assets.
Wrong: buying and selling without paying.
Wrong: trading ahead of customer orders.

questions.q: For which investor is a fee-based account LEAST suitable?
o: An active trader placing many orders
A client with a large portfolio and frequent rebalancing
A buy-and-hold investor who trades rarely
w: Fits a fee-based account.
This investor suits a fee-based account: fees are predictable rather than per-trade.
This investor suits a fee-based account: frequent activity makes a flat or asset-based fee efficient.
Correct: a rare trader pays fees for little activity.

questions.q: Two siblings open a joint account and each wants their share to go to their own spouse at death. Which title fits?
w: Wrong: the survivor would take everything.
Wrong: it needs two owners.
Correct: JTIC lets each owner’s share pass to their own beneficiary.
Wrong: custodial account for a minor.

questions.q: Which account avoids probate at an owner’s death?
w: Wrong: JTIC shares are probated.
Correct: assets pass directly to the survivor.
Wrong: goes through the estate unless TOD is designated.
Wrong: corporations have unlimited life, probate does not apply.

questions.q: In a joint account, which statement is correct?
o: Any owner may give trading instructions, but checks must be payable to all owners
Checks may be made out to any one owner
All owners must sign every order
A parent and a minor child may open one
w: Correct: any owner may instruct the firm, but checks must be payable to all owners.
Wrong: checks must name all owners.
Wrong: one owner may give instructions.
Wrong: a minor cannot be part of a joint account.

questions.q: Which statement about UGMA/UTMA accounts is TRUE?
o: The minor may trade with the custodian’s permission
The custodian’s Social Security number is on the account
Margin trading is permitted with the custodian’s approval
Gifts to the account are irrevocable
w: Wrong: the minor cannot trade.
Wrong: the minor’s number is used.
Wrong: margin is not permitted.
Correct: the donor cannot take the gift back.

questions.q: Who owes the income tax on dividends earned in a UTMA account?
w: Wrong: the custodian ensures payment but is not liable.
Correct: the minor owns the assets and is liable for taxes.
Wrong: the broker-dealer is not the taxpayer; the minor owns the assets and owes the tax.
Wrong: the gift is irrevocable.

questions.q: John buys XYZ at $10 and dies when it trades at $30. His daughter inherits and later sells at $34. What is her taxable gain per share?
w: Correct: stepped-up basis of $30; gain = $34 − $30.
Wrong: $30 − $10 is the deceased’s gain.
Wrong: uses the original basis.
Wrong: the full proceeds.

questions.q: What document must a corporation provide to open a brokerage account?
o: A copy of the articles of incorporation only
A corporate resolution naming persons authorized to trade
A power of attorney from each shareholder
w: Wrong: insufficient to name authorized traders.
Wrong: used for partnerships.
Correct: the board resolution names who may transact.
Wrong: shareholders do not grant authority; the board names the authorised traders by resolution.

questions.q: A customer account holds stocks and penny stocks and has recent activity. How often must the firm send statements?
w: Wrong: there is no annual-statement rule; statements are at least quarterly, monthly with penny stocks or options.
Wrong: quarterly applies to ordinary accounts.
Correct: holding options or penny stocks triggers monthly statements.
Wrong: required with any position or activity.

questions.q: A trade confirmation must be sent to the customer:
o: At or before completion of the transaction
w: Wrong: confirmations are mandatory.
Wrong: 30 days is far too late; the confirmation is due no later than settlement.
Wrong: after settlement is too late; confirmations are due at or before settlement.
Correct: at or before settlement.

questions.q: On a principal (dealer) trade with a retail customer, the confirmation must show:
w: Wrong: commission applies to agency trades.
Correct: a principal trade must show the mark-up or mark-down.
Wrong: the firm’s net capital is not shown on a trade confirmation.
Wrong: the mark-up/mark-down must be disclosed.

questions.q: A customer asks the firm to hold mail for 5 months because he doesn’t want to deal with it. The firm should:
o: Refuse because convenience is not an acceptable reason beyond 3 months
w: Correct: beyond three months a valid reason such as safety is required.
Wrong: written instruction is necessary but not enough here.
Wrong: approval does not change the rule.
Wrong: a hold request must be in writing, and the length is the problem here.

questions.q: For how long must a firm keep customer account records after the account is closed?
w: Wrong: one year is far shorter than the six-year retention requirement.
Wrong: three years falls short; the requirement is six years after closing.
Correct: at least six years after closing.
Wrong: retention is six years after closing, not indefinite.

questions.q: Under Regulation S-P, a customer cannot opt out of information sharing:
o: When the notice was sent annually
When the sharing is required by law, such as in an AML investigation
w: Wrong: this is what opt-out is for.
Wrong: the annual notice does not remove or create an opt-out right; legally required sharing is the exception.
Wrong: not the typical test.
Correct: legally required sharing cannot be blocked.

questions.q: Using customer fully paid securities as collateral for the firm’s own loan is:
w: Correct: fully paid securities must be segregated.
Wrong: hypothecation applies to margin securities under an agreement.
Wrong: fully paid securities must be segregated; notice does not make pledging them for the firm’s debt legal.
Wrong: listing status is irrelevant; commingling fully paid securities is prohibited.

questions.q: An investor has $100,000 of securities and $300,000 cash in a brokerage account when the firm fails. What is the maximum SIPC protection?
w: Wrong: ignores the cash cap.
Correct: securities $100,000 + cash capped at $250,000.
Wrong: the $500,000 limit isn’t reached.
Wrong: the cash cap, not the total.

questions.q: An investor holds an individual account, a joint account with a spouse, and a Roth IRA at the same firm. For SIPC, how many separate customers are there?
w: Wrong: dollar amounts determine the limit, not the number of separate customers.
Wrong: three different account titles, not two.
Wrong: one customer would apply only if all assets sat in a single account title.
Correct: each account type is a separate customer, each protected to the limit.

questions.q: Which statement correctly contrasts FDIC and SIPC?
o: FDIC covers bank deposits; SIPC covers securities and cash at a failed broker-dealer
SIPC is a US government agency
FDIC protects market losses, SIPC does not
w: Correct: FDIC insures bank deposits; SIPC covers securities and cash at a failed broker-dealer.
Wrong: SIPC is a non-profit corporation.
Wrong: neither covers market losses.
Wrong: neither covers fund losses.

questions.q: A firm reasonably believes a 70-year-old customer is being financially exploited. What can the firm do first?
o: Place a temporary hold on disbursements for up to 15 business days
w: Wrong: reports go to adult protective services or state regulators; the first action is the hold.
Correct: initial 15-business-day hold.
Wrong: a firm cannot close the account on suspicion; the rule allows a temporary hold on disbursements.
Wrong: indefinite freezes are not authorized.

questions.q: SIPC protects an investor against:
o: A decline in the value of securities
The failure of the brokerage firm
w: Wrong: market losses are not covered.
Wrong: poor advice is a suitability/regulatory matter, not covered by SIPC.
Correct: SIPC steps in when the brokerage firm fails.
Wrong: commodities and futures are not covered.
